Introduce the proposal as a connected customer website and workshop workspace. The deck shows the current prototype and the business workflow it is designed to support. This is a product prototype. Calendar and message workflows run locally in the browser. A production release needs a backend, authentication and configured service connections. WhatsApp conversation shown in simulation. Live delivery requires the company’s API connection.

Screenshots: local DC Motors website and admin prototype, captured 26 October 2026. All customer records and prices are fictional demonstration data. Screens use prepared local demo states. This slide shows the WhatsApp bot conversation simulator in the admin request detail and the corresponding customer tracking view. The flow supports YES, NO, ANOTHER TIME, numbered time options, common phrases and staff follow-up for unclear replies. The system rechecks availability before confirmation. Actual WhatsApp delivery needs the company Business Platform connection, approved templates where required and a server-side webhook. The customer reference/phone lookup is only a local demonstration. title: What this means for DC Motors

text: What this means for DC Motors
Product prototype
A clearer enquiry path
Customers can move from the right service to a relevant request.
Less repeated information
Customer and vehicle details stay with the enquiry and job.
Better scheduling visibility
Staff can compare provisional requests with confirmed work.
More consistent follow-up
Suggested times and decisions share one request history.

These are intended qualitative benefits of the proposed workflow, not measured savings or revenue guarantees. Use them to invite the client to explain their present booking and workshop process. Suggested pilot measures: submitted requests, response time, confirmed appointments, reschedules and staff feedback. Do not invent targets without a baseline.
A controlled path to launch
Product prototype

The prototype makes the customer journey
and workshop workflow ready to review
Agree the operating rules
Confirm services, visit durations, resources and approval responsibilities.
Connect the live services
Add secure accounts, shared data and the company WhatsApp connection.
Pilot with the workshop team
Test real scheduling scenarios, customer replies and staff handoffs.
Launch and measure
Use approved content and review enquiry handling and booking outcomes.

Close by agreeing the next scope decisions, not by implying the prototype is already live. The demonstrated local workflows can guide the production implementation. Production needs backend persistence, authenticated roles, secure customer tracking, WhatsApp integration and real delivery handling. Confirm whether invoice payment remains with the existing billing provider. Agree approved client photography, content and scheduling rules. A pilot should test real workshop processes before a public release. This is a product prototype. Calendar and message workflows run locally in the browser. A production release needs a backend, authentication and configured service connections. No live WhatsApp messages or payments have been sent.
